title: Processes, as deep as data needs
sub: Business architecture for data, the second series on enterprise architecture: the utility's processes in four bands and in levels, from the macro processes on the map to each process with its trigger, output and owner, and its activities as a flow only where something hurts; a SIPOC for each process, naming the concepts it reads and writes, and so where each one is born; and the step, drawn in BPMN, where an estimated reading is born.
howto: Glass in the layers' colours is the confirmed model: yellow is the business layer, where the processes sit, and salmon the information layer, where the business's concepts sit. Levels go down the screen: level one, the macro processes; level two, the processes under each; level three, a flow of activities, drawn only where it hurts. A dashed outline marks a branch that wasn't drawn deeper, or a concept not yet on the map. Gold marks an owner; blue the data team. In the desert, blue is the water, and the people of the story are silhouettes.
